item.title: Go 2026 Survival Guide for Backend Engineers: The Changes That Actually Affect Production
item.description: Go 1.25 and 1.26 bring container-aware GOMAXPROCS, go fix overhaul, Green Tea GC, testing/synctest, and more. A practical breakdown of what backend engineers actually need to know.

item.title: Rust 10x Faster Than Spring? I Ran the Benchmarks. The Truth Is More Complicated.
item.description: Behind the benchmark numbers are three competing models: GC pauses, JIT warmup, and AOT compilation. Here's the data-driven breakdown of when to use Rust versus when Quarkus Native Image is the smarter choice.

item.title: From 1GB to 40MB: How Rust Cracks Memory Management
item.description: Same microservice, same endpoints, but memory usage dropped from 1GB to 40MB after rewriting Node.js to Rust. That's 25x less memory. How does Rust pull this off? Let's talk about ownership.

item.title: From Zero to 1.8M Connections: A Rust/Tokio Gateway's Real Scaling Journey
item.description: This isn't a Rust success story about how fast it is. It's a postmortem about when concurrent connections cross from hundreds of thousands to millions, schedulers, backpressure, and observability matter more than raw efficiency.

item.title: 4000 Pages Per Second: The Rust PDF Library That's Changing the Game
item.description: oxidize-pdf: A pure-Rust PDF engine with zero C dependencies, a 5MB binary, and performance that leaves Chromium and Java stacks in the dust.

item.title: Xiao Li Rewrote Go Monolith to Rust Axum, Company Saved $800K+ Yearly, His Salary Hit $2M
item.description: This isn't a story about flexing how fast Rust is. It's about how tech choices translate to real money, and why most rewrite projects can't replicate this result.

item.title: Rust Design Patterns: 3 Best Practices Senior Backend Engineers Always Use
item.description: Discover the Rust design patterns senior engineers swear by: Newtype pattern prevents invalid states, ownership design reflects system boundaries, enum error handling makes failures predictable. Master these Rust best practices to build rock-solid backend code and say goodbye to midnight incidents.

item.title: gRPC is 10x Faster Than REST? Why Your Team Hasn't Switched
item.description: gRPC can indeed be much faster than REST, but most teams are right to stick with REST. Let's talk about the real cost behind the speed.

item.title: Rust System Design: These Three Libraries Quietly Do the Dirty Work (And Many Devs Still Don’t Know)
item.description: Tokio, Crossbeam, and Rkyv: three crates that make concurrency, state sharing, and serialization dramatically simpler in Rust.

item.title: I Fired My Entire Node.js Stack — Rust Rebuilt It in 3 Weeks (The Ugly Truth)
item.description: API latency dropped from 850ms to 8ms, monthly costs from $12,000 to $900. Sounds great? The price was three months of hell and a team on the verge of collapse. This is a real backend migration story.

item.title: I Thought Rust Was Over-Engineering—Until I Saw the Production Logs
item.description: A 2 AM production incident made me rethink Rust. From 8 crashes per hour to zero crashes—this isn't about language wars, it's about trust.

item.title: Rust Performance Optimization: 7 Underused Features Every Senior Developer Knows
item.description: Deep dive into 7 underrated Rust features for systems programming performance optimization. From p99 latency tuning to memory management, these advanced Rust techniques will make your production code perform better.
